ai.title: System prompt file tree truncation fallback
ai.summary: Added `else` branch in `truncateFileTreeBasedOnTokenBudget` (`backend/src/system-prompt.ts`) to return root-only directory tree when token budget exhaustion prevents standard truncation. Renamed `line` to `patchLine` in `applyPatch` (`common/src/util/patch.ts`) to resolve shadowing conflicts with `parseHunk` context variables. Scope limited to core prompt assembly and patch utility internals. No user-facing behavior change; ensures valid tree structure persists under strict token limits.

eli5.text: When the system assembles a list of files to show you, it usually trims that list down if it gets too long for the space allowed. Now, if trimming would still leave the list too big, it falls back to showing just the top-level folder names instead of the whole expanded tree. You'd only notice this while interacting with a project that has a very large nested file structure under tight space constraints, and even then, you'd simply see a collapsed root view rather than nothing at all. A separate behind-the-scenes tweak renamed a temporary variable in the patch-handling logic to avoid confusing overlaps; there's no effect to observe.

ai.title: Add Drizzle ORM PostgreSQL backend
ai.summary: Integrated Drizzle ORM 0.33.0 and postgres.js 3.4.4 for backend database management. New schema defines a users table with serial id, unique varchar email, and timestamp created_at. Migrations generated in backend/src/db/drizzle; setup requires Cloud SQL proxy via mac-cloud-sql-proxy binary and DATABASE_URL env var.

eli5.text: The application can now save and look up information about people who sign up, using a proper database system hosted on Google Cloud. When you start the application, it automatically connects to a secure tunnel to that database and begins tracking each person with a unique ID, their email address, and the date they joined. If you look at the project's setup notes, you'll see new instructions for developers on how to connect to this database locally using a Google-provided credential file and a tunneling tool.
